assessments.reasoning: Oracle’s HTTPS response returned HTTP 200 for both acquisitions. The reported whole-body and range digests matched the supplied pins, and [0,9217) and [9217,18435) covered the response contiguously. Agreement text occupies [0,17901), from “COMMON DEVELOPMENT AND DISTRIBUTION LICENSE (CDDL) Version 1.1” through Section 10’s final words, “any admission of liability.” Two line feeds precede the 72 hyphens at [17903,17975), and two more precede the notice at byte 17977. The notice specifies California law excluding conflict-of-law provisions, jurisdiction in the Federal Courts of the Northern District of California and the state courts of the State of California, and venue in Santa Clara County, California. Two final line feeds close the response.

Both HTTP 200 responses came from the SPDX repository’s commit-pinned text/CDDL-1.1.txt URL. Their reported whole-body and range digests matched the supplied pins, and [0,8695) and [8695,17390) covered the file contiguously. SPDX puts Version 1.1 on its own line, uses typographic quotation marks, and carries the same notice immediately after Section 10 with no hyphen rule. The full ordered token comparison confirmed the wording through the final venue sentence.

The complete 700-byte HTTP 200 response from the SPDX repository’s GitHub Git objects endpoint matched the pinned response digest. It identifies annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b as v3.29.0 and gives its target type as commit and target SHA as 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48, exactly the revision in the acquired text URL. The API reports the tag as unsigned.

challenge.method: Ran the supplied JavaScript unchanged on the freshly acquired parts. It joined each pair with join(""), folded curly quotation marks to straight marks, tokenized on spaces, tabs, carriage returns, and line feeds, and filtered the exact 72-hyphen token from Oracle. It compared ordered tokens with the notice retained, then compared Oracle’s prefix before the notice against the complete SPDX text. For the changed-clause control, spdx.replace("License Grants", "License Conditions") changed the Section 2 heading before token comparison.
challenge.results: Observed byte_identical=false, normalized_with_notice=true, normalized_agreement_only=false, publisher_notice=true, spdx_notice=true, separator_count=1, and altered_clause_equal=false. Removing the Oracle notice broke the match to the complete SPDX file. The changed Section 2 heading also broke the match.

limitations: The finding covers the two exact captures and the specified normalization. It establishes neither byte equality nor equivalence to another CDDL edition.

Section 9 refers to a notice contained within the Original Software. The attached California notice is a project-specific representation that applies by its own terms. The crosswalk does not assign it to unrelated projects or determine any project's license applicability or approval classification.
The upstream annotated tag is unsigned. Its release-to-commit mapping is supported by the pinned GitHub API response.

Review scope is descriptive under SCES-1.0 ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710 and policy digest 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce. Canonical admission, redistribution, and publication are outside this finding.
reasoning: At the commit targeted by SPDX v3.29.0, text/CDDL-1.1.txt matches Oracle’s Version 1.1 agreement and attached Section 9 notice under the specified JavaScript normalization. Both headings explicitly identify Version 1.1, and Section 4.1 names Oracle as the initial license steward. The complete texts differ in byte length, line wrapping, indentation, quotation marks, and the visual separator.

reproduction.reason: The independent execution ran the exact pinned JavaScript procedure on the complete acquired sources and reproduced the comparison and changed-clause control.
